title: Transformations
overview: Every polynomial graph in this section is a familiar power function, $y = x^n$, that has been stretched, compressed, reflected or slid. Learn what each parameter in $y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$ does, and you can sketch complicated-looking graphs in seconds, write equations from descriptions, and read the vertex, symmetry and range straight from an equation.
objectives: Identify the parameters $a$, $k$, $d$, $c$ and describe the transformation each represents.
Apply transformations in the correct order to sketch $y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$.
Map points using $(x, y) \to (\tfrac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c)$.
Write an equation from a description of transformations.
State the domain and range, and for even powers the vertex and axis of symmetry.

lessons.title: The four parameters a, k, d and c
lessons.body:
Every graph in this section starts from a **power function** $y = x^n$ and is moved and reshaped using

$$y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$$

| Parameter | Effect | Mapping of a point $(x, y)$ |
|---|---|---|
| $a$ | vertical stretch by factor $\lvert a\rvert$ if $\lvert a\rvert > 1$, compression if $0 < \lvert a\rvert < 1$; **reflection in the $x$-axis** if $a < 0$ | $y \to ay$ |
| $k$ | horizontal compression by factor $\tfrac{1}{\lvert k\rvert}$ if $\lvert k\rvert > 1$, stretch if $0 < \lvert k\rvert < 1$; **reflection in the $y$-axis** if $k < 0$ | $x \to \tfrac{x}{k}$ |
| $d$ | horizontal translation: right if $d > 0$, left if $d < 0$ | $x \to x + d$ |
| $c$ | vertical translation: up if $c > 0$, down if $c < 0$ | $y \to y + c$ |

All four together: $(x, y) \to \left(\dfrac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c\right)$.

> **Watch the signs.** In $y = [2(x + 1)]^3$, $d = -1$ (because $x + 1 = x - (-1)$), so the shift is 1 unit **left**.

**Order of transformations.** Apply stretches, compressions and reflections ($a$ and $k$) *before* translations ($c$ and $d$) — the same order as BEDMAS: multiply first, then add.

lessons.title: Sketching with a table of key points
Even powers: vertex, axis of symmetry and range
lessons.body:
When $n$ is even, $y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$ looks like a (flatter) parabola:

* the **vertex** is $(d, c)$;
* the **axis of symmetry** is $x = d$;
* if $a > 0$ it opens **up**, the vertex is a minimum, and the range is $\{y \in \mathbb{R},\ y \ge c\}$;
* if $a < 0$ it opens **down**, the vertex is a maximum, and the range is $\{y \in \mathbb{R},\ y \le c\}$.

```plot
title: y = x⁴ and y = −0.5(x − 2)⁴ + 3
f: x^4 | label=y = x⁴
f: -0.5*(x-2)^4 + 3 | label=y = −0.5(x − 2)⁴ + 3
domain: -2, 4.5
range: -5, 6
points: (2,3)
asymptote x: 2
```

(The dashed line marks the axis of symmetry $x = 2$.)

For odd $n$ there is no vertex and the domain and range are both all real numbers; the point $(d, c)$ is the centre of point symmetry (where $y = x^3$'s origin moves to).

lessons.title: Writing equations from descriptions
lessons.body:
Translate each phrase into a parameter, then substitute into $y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$.

| Phrase | Parameter |
|---|---|
| "vertically stretched by a factor of 5" | $a = 5$ |
| "vertically compressed by a factor of $\tfrac34$" | $a = \tfrac34$ |
| "reflected in the $x$-axis" | make $a$ negative |
| "horizontally compressed by a factor of $\tfrac13$" | $k = 3$ |
| "horizontally stretched by a factor of 2" | $k = \tfrac12$ |
| "reflected in the $y$-axis" | make $k$ negative |
| "translated 4 units left" | $d = -4$ |
| "translated 7 units up" | $c = 7$ |

**Example.** $y = x^4$ is compressed vertically by a factor of $\tfrac13$, stretched horizontally by a factor of 2, reflected in the $y$-axis, and translated 1 unit up and 4 units left.

$a = \tfrac13$, $k = -\tfrac12$, $d = -4$, $c = 1$:
$$y = \tfrac13\left[-\tfrac12(x + 4)\right]^4 + 1$$

Vertex $(-4, 1)$, axis $x = -4$, opens up, range $\{y \ge 1\}$. (Because the power is even, the reflection in the $y$-axis has no visible effect.)

lessons.title: Factor out k before reading d
lessons.body:
An equation like $y = -(2x + 6)^4$ hides the horizontal translation. Factor the coefficient of $x$ out of the bracket first:

$$y = -(2x + 6)^4 = -[2(x + 3)]^4$$

Now read $k = 2$ (horizontal compression by $\tfrac12$), $d = -3$ (3 units left), $a = -1$ (reflection in the $x$-axis). Vertex $(-3, 0)$.

> A common error is to read "6 left" from $(2x + 6)$. The shift is $\dfrac{6}{2} = 3$.

**Useful identity.** For a power function, a horizontal compression can be rewritten as a vertical stretch: $(kx)^n = k^n x^n$. So $y = (2x)^3$ is the same graph as $y = 8x^3$.

keyTerms.definition: A function of the form $y = ax^n$, where $n$ is a whole number.
A change in position, size or orientation of a graph: translation, stretch, compression or reflection.
Sliding a graph left/right ($d$) or up/down ($c$) without changing its shape.
For even $n$, the turning point $(d, c)$ of $y=a[k(x-d)]^n+c$.
The vertical line $x = d$ through the vertex of an even-power graph.

formulas.name: Point mapping
formulas.meaning: Where each point of $y = x^n$ moves.

workedExamples.title: Describe the transformations
workedExamples.problem: Describe how $y = x^4$ is transformed to obtain $y = 4[3(x + 2)]^4$, and state the domain, range, vertex and axis of symmetry.
steps: $k = 3$: horizontal compression by a factor of $\tfrac13$. $a = 4$: vertical stretch by a factor of 4.
$d = -2$: translation 2 units left. No vertical translation.
Vertex $(-2, 0)$, axis of symmetry $x = -2$. $a > 0$ so it opens up: range $\{y \in \mathbb{R},\ y \ge 0\}$, domain $\{x \in \mathbb{R}\}$.
workedExamples.answer: Compress horizontally by $\tfrac13$, stretch vertically by 4, shift 2 left; vertex $(-2,0)$.

workedExamples.title: Map a point
workedExamples.problem: Where does the point $(2, 8)$ on $y = x^3$ go under $y = -3[2(x + 1)]^3 + 5$?
steps: Use $(x, y) \to (\tfrac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c)$ with $a=-3$, $k=2$, $d=-1$, $c=5$.

workedExamples.title: Equation from a description
workedExamples.problem: $y = x^3$ is compressed horizontally by a factor of $\tfrac13$, stretched vertically by a factor of 5, reflected in the $x$-axis, and translated 2 units left and 7 units up. Write the equation.
steps: Vertical stretch by 5 with reflection in the $x$-axis → $a = -5$.
workedExamples.answer: $y = -5[3(x + 2)]^3 + 7$; domain and range are all real numbers.

workedExamples.title: Factor first
workedExamples.problem: Describe $y = -(2x + 6)^4$ as a transformation of $y = x^4$.
steps: $k = 2$: horizontal compression by $\tfrac12$. $a = -1$: reflection in the $x$-axis. $d = -3$: 3 units left.
workedExamples.answer: Compress horizontally by ½, reflect in the $x$-axis, shift 3 left.

workedExamples.title: Equation from a graph
workedExamples.problem:
The graph is a transformation of $y = x^3$. Its centre of symmetry is $(1, 3)$ and it also passes through $(2, 3.5)$. Find its equation in the form $y = a(x - d)^3 + c$.

```plot
f: 0.5*(x-1)^3 + 3
domain: -2, 4
range: -6, 10
points: (1,3), (2,3.5), (0,2.5)
```
steps: The point $(0,0)$ of $y = x^3$ has moved to $(1, 3)$: $d = 1$, $c = 3$.
workedExamples.answer: $y = 0.5(x - 1)^3 + 3$ — a vertical compression by ½, then 1 right and 3 up.

misconceptions.fact: $k = 2$ **compresses** horizontally by a factor of $\tfrac12$ (divide $x$-coordinates by 2).
Factor first: $[2(x + 3)]^4$, so the shift is 3 left.
Stretches, compressions and reflections ($a$, $k$) come before translations ($c$, $d$).

misconceptions.myth: Reflecting $y = x^4$ in the $y$-axis changes the graph.
misconceptions.fact: $y = x^4$ is symmetric about the $y$-axis, so a reflection in the $y$-axis leaves it unchanged.

realWorld.title: Graphic and product design
realWorld.body: Designers build curves for logos, furniture and car bodies by stretching and shifting simple power curves, keeping track of the vertex and symmetry.

realWorld.title: Animation
realWorld.body: Computer animation moves a shape by applying the same point mapping $(x, y) \to (x/k + d,\ ay + c)$ to every vertex.

realWorld.title: Engineering profiles
realWorld.body: A bowl or lamp-shade cross-section might be modelled by $y = a(x - d)^4 + c$: the vertex gives the depth and $d$ the centre line.

practice.question: State the parameters and transformations for $y = 2\left[\tfrac13(x - 5)\right]^4$ from $y = x^4$.
practice.solution: $a = 2$: vertical stretch by 2. $k = \tfrac13$: horizontal stretch by 3. $d = 5$: 5 right. Vertex $(5, 0)$, axis $x = 5$, range $y \ge 0$.

practice.question: Write the equation: $y = x^4$ stretched vertically by 3, reflected in the $x$-axis, translated 2 right and 5 up. State the range.
Rewrite $y = (3x)^3$ as a vertical stretch.
practice.solution: $y = 27x^3$: a vertical stretch by a factor of 27.

practice.question: Explain which parameters change the shape of a graph and which only change its position.
practice.solution: $a$ and $k$ change the shape (stretch, compress) and may reflect it. $c$ and $d$ only slide the graph without changing its shape.

summary: $y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$ transforms $y = x^n$: $a$ vertical stretch/reflection, $k$ horizontal stretch/reflection, $d$ horizontal shift, $c$ vertical shift.
Points map as $(x, y) \to (\tfrac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c)$.
For even $n$: vertex $(d, c)$, axis $x = d$, range $y \ge c$ ($a>0$) or $y \le c$ ($a<0$). For odd $n$: domain and range are all real numbers.
Factor the coefficient of $x$ out of the bracket before reading $d$.

questions.text: The graph of $y = x^4$ is transformed to obtain $y = {{a}}[{{k}}(x - {{d}})]^4 + {{c}}$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the vertex and the equation of the axis of symmetry. Give the $x$-coordinate of the vertex.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the domain and range. Give the minimum value.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $a = {{a}}$: vertical stretch by a factor of {{a}}. $k = {{k}}$: horizontal compression by a factor of $\tfrac{1}{ {{k}} }$. $d = {{d}}$: translation {{d}} units right. $c = {{c}}$: translation {{c}} units up. (Apply the stretch and compression first, then the translations.)

(b) Vertex $({{d}}, {{c}})$; axis of symmetry $x = {{d}}$.

(c) Domain $\{x \in \mathbb{R}\}$. Since $a > 0$ the graph opens up and the vertex is a minimum: range $\{y \in \mathbb{R},\ y \ge {{c}}\}$.

questions.text: The point $(2, 8)$ lies on $y = x^3$. Determine the coordinates of its image on $y = {{a}}[{{k}}(x - {{d}})]^3 + {{c}}$, and explain each step.
questions.modelAnswer:
Use the mapping $(x, y) \to \left(\dfrac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c\right)$.

$x$: $\dfrac{2}{ {{k}} } + {{d}} = {{2/k + d}}$ (horizontal compression, then shift right).

$y$: ${{a}}(8) + {{c}} = {{8*a + c}}$ (vertical stretch, then shift up).

Image: $\left({{2/k + d}},\ {{8*a + c}}\right)$.

questions.text: The function $y = x^3$ is stretched vertically by a factor of {{a}}, reflected in the $x$-axis, compressed horizontally by a factor of $\tfrac{1}{ {{k}} }$, and translated {{d}} units right and {{c}} units down.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation of the transformed function.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Determine the image of the point $(1, 1)$. Give the $y$-coordinate.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $a = -{{a}}$, $k = {{k}}$, $d = {{d}}$, $c = -{{c}}$:
$$y = -{{a}}[{{k}}(x - {{d}})]^3 - {{c}}$$

(b) The point $(1, 1)$ maps to $\left(\dfrac{1}{ {{k}} } + {{d}},\ -{{a}}(1) - {{c}}\right) = \left({{1/k + d:3}},\ {{-a - c}}\right)$.

(c) Domain $\{x \in \mathbb{R}\}$, range $\{y \in \mathbb{R}\}$ — an odd power function's domain and range are unchanged by these transformations.

questions.text: Explain why, when sketching $y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$, the stretches, compressions and reflections must be applied before the translations. Use the point $(1, 1)$ on $y = x^3$ and the function $y = 2(x - 3)^3$ to show what goes wrong if the order is reversed.
questions.modelAnswer:
Every point on the transformed graph is found from a point on $y = x^n$ with the rule $(x, y) \to \left(\tfrac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c\right)$. Like the order of operations (BEDMAS), the multiplications — stretches, compressions and reflections ($a$, $k$) — are done first, and the additions — translations ($c$, $d$) — last.

Correct for $y = 2(x - 3)^3$: $(1, 1)$ → stretch vertically by 2 → $(1, 2)$ → shift 3 right → $(4, 2)$. Check: $2(4 - 3)^3 = 2$ ✓.

Reversed order for $y = 2x^3 + 5$: shifting $(1, 1)$ up 5 gives $(1, 6)$, then stretching by 2 gives $(1, 12)$. But substituting, $2(1)^3 + 5 = 7$, so the correct image is $(1, 7)$ — stretch first, then shift. Translating first wrongly stretches the translation as well.

rubric.point: Links order to order of operations
Correct worked image using the right order
Shows a wrong result from reversing the order and checks by substitution

questions.text: Describe the function $y = -({{k}}x + {{k*d}})^4$ as a transformation of $y = x^4$. State the vertex, the axis of symmetry and the range.
questions.modelAnswer:
Factor the bracket: ${{k}}x + {{k*d}} = {{k}}(x + {{d}})$, so $y = -[{{k}}(x + {{d}})]^4$.

* $k = {{k}}$: horizontal compression by a factor of $\tfrac{1}{ {{k}} }$.
* $a = -1$: reflection in the $x$-axis.
* $d = -{{d}}$: translation {{d}} units left (not {{k*d}}!).

Vertex $(-{{d}}, 0)$; axis of symmetry $x = -{{d}}$. Opens down: range $\{y \in \mathbb{R},\ y \le 0\}$.

rubric.point: Factors k out of the bracket

parts.label: a
parts.text: Does the graph have a maximum or minimum point? State its value.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the equation of the axis of symmetry.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $n$ is even, $a = -{{a}} < 0$: the graph opens **down**, so the vertex $(-{{d}}, {{c}})$ is a **maximum** point. The maximum value is {{c}}.

(b) Axis of symmetry: $x = -{{d}}$.

(c) Domain $\{x \in \mathbb{R}\}$; range $\{y \in \mathbb{R},\ y \le {{c}}\}$.

(d) $f(0) = -{{a}}[{{k}}({{d}})]^4 + {{c}} = {{-a*(k*d)^4 + c}}$.

questions.text:
The graph shown is a transformation of $y = x^3$ of the form $y = a(x - d)^3 + c$. The marked points are the image of the origin and the image of $(1, 1)$.

```plot
f: {{1*a}}*(x-{{d}})^3 + {{c}}
domain: {{d}}-2.5, {{d}}+2.5
points: ({{d}},{{c}}), ({{d}}+1,{{a+c}})
```
questions.modelAnswer:
The origin of $y = x^3$ (its centre of symmetry) moves to $({{d}}, {{c}})$, so $d = {{d}}$ and $c = {{c}}$.

The point $(1, 1)$ moves to $(1 + d,\ a + c) = ({{d+1}}, {{a+c}})$, so $a + {{c}} = {{a+c}}$ and $a = {{1*a}}$.

$$y = {{1*a}}(x - {{d}})^3 + {{c}}$$

Transformations: vertical stretch by a factor of {{1*a}}, then {{d}} units right and {{c}} units up.

rubric.point: Identifies d and c from the centre point
Uses second point to find a

questions.text: Explain why reflecting $y = x^3$ in the $y$-axis gives the same graph as reflecting it in the $x$-axis, but reflecting $y = x^4$ in the $y$-axis leaves it unchanged. Use algebra to support your explanation.
questions.modelAnswer:
Reflection in the $y$-axis replaces $x$ with $-x$; reflection in the $x$-axis multiplies $y$ by $-1$.

* $y = x^3$: reflecting in the $y$-axis gives $y = (-x)^3 = -x^3$, which is exactly the reflection in the $x$-axis. This happens because $x^3$ is an **odd** function: $f(-x) = -f(x)$.
* $y = x^4$: reflecting in the $y$-axis gives $y = (-x)^4 = x^4$ — the same function. $x^4$ is an **even** function, symmetric about the $y$-axis, so the mirror image is itself.

rubric.point: States what each reflection does algebraically

questions.text: Show that $y = ({{k}}x)^4$ can be described either as a horizontal compression or as a vertical stretch of $y = x^4$. State both factors.
questions.modelAnswer:
As written, $k = {{k}}$: a **horizontal compression** by a factor of $\tfrac{1}{ {{k}} }$.

Using exponent laws, $({{k}}x)^4 = {{k}}^4x^4 = {{k^4}}x^4$, so the same graph is a **vertical stretch** by a factor of {{k^4}}.

Check with a point: on $y = ({{k}}x)^4$, $x = 1$ gives $y = {{k^4}}$, and on $y = {{k^4}}x^4$, $x = 1$ gives ${{k^4}}$ ✓.

questions.text: Determine the $x$-intercept of $g(x) = {{a}}(x - {{d}})^3 - {{c}}$, correct to two decimal places. Explain why a transformed cubic of this form has exactly one $x$-intercept.
questions.modelAnswer:
Set $g(x) = 0$:
$${{a}}(x - {{d}})^3 = {{c}} \;\Rightarrow\; (x - {{d}})^3 = \frac{ {{c}} }{ {{a}} } \;\Rightarrow\; x = {{d}} + \sqrt[3]{\frac{ {{c}} }{ {{a}} }} \approx {{d + (c/a)^(1/3):3}}$$

Exactly one intercept: $y = x^3$ is always increasing, and stretching and translating keep it always increasing (since $a > 0$), so the graph crosses each horizontal line — including the $x$-axis — exactly once.

questions.text: The function $y = x^4$ is compressed vertically by a factor of $\tfrac13$, stretched horizontally by a factor of 2, reflected in the $y$-axis, and translated 1 unit up and 4 units to the left.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the vertex, axis of symmetry, domain and range. Give the minimum value.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain whether the reflection changes the graph.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) $a = \tfrac13$, $k = -\tfrac12$, $d = -4$, $c = 1$:
$$y = \tfrac13\left[-\tfrac12(x + 4)\right]^4 + 1$$

(b) Vertex $(-4, 1)$, axis $x = -4$. $a > 0$: opens up, so range $\{y \in \mathbb{R},\ y \ge 1\}$; domain $\{x \in \mathbb{R}\}$.

(c) The reflection in the $y$-axis has no visible effect because $[-\tfrac12(x+4)]^4 = [\tfrac12(x+4)]^4$ (an even power removes the negative sign).

rubric.point: Correct a and k (including the negative k)
Explains the y-axis reflection has no effect

questions.text: A designer models the cross-section of a bowl with $y = a(x - {{d}})^4$, where $a = {{s/100}}$, $x$ and $y$ are in centimetres, and the rim of the bowl is at height $y = {{h}}$ cm.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the vertex and axis of symmetry.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve for the $x$-values at the rim.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Determine the width of the bowl at the rim.

questions.modelAnswer:
(a) Vertex $({{d}}, 0)$: the bottom of the bowl is at $x = {{d}}$ cm, depth measured from $y=0$. The axis of symmetry is $x = {{d}}$.

(b) Set $y = {{h}}$:
$$(x - {{d}})^4 = \frac{ {{h}} }{ {{s/100}} } \Rightarrow x - {{d}} = \pm\left(\frac{ {{h}} }{ {{s/100}} }\right)^{1/4} \approx \pm{{(h/(0.01*s))^(0.25):3}}$$

(c) Width of the rim $= 2 \times {{(h/(0.01*s))^(0.25):3}} \approx {{2*(h/(0.01*s))^(0.25):3}}$ cm.

rubric.point: Sets up equation at rim height
Solves using a fourth root, both signs

questions.text: Under $y = 2\left[-\tfrac13(x - 1)\right]^3 - 4$, determine the images of the points $(-2, -8)$, $(0, 0)$ and $(3, 27)$ on $y = x^3$.
questions.modelAnswer:
Parameters: $a = 2$, $k = -\tfrac13$, $d = 1$, $c = -4$. Mapping: $(x, y) \to \left(\dfrac{x}{k} + d,\ ay + c\right) = (-3x + 1,\ 2y - 4)$.

* $(-2, -8) \to (6 + 1,\ -16 - 4) = (7, -20)$
* $(0, 0) \to (1, -4)$
* $(3, 27) \to (-9 + 1,\ 54 - 4) = (-8, 50)$

Note the reflection in the $y$-axis ($k<0$) sends points with negative $x$ to the right side.

questions.text: Which parameters in $y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$ change the **shape** of a power function's graph, and which change only its **position**? Which can produce reflections? Give an example of each.
questions.modelAnswer:
* **Shape:** $a$ (vertical stretch/compression) and $k$ (horizontal stretch/compression). Example: $y = 3x^4$ is narrower than $y = x^4$; $y = (0.5x)^4$ is wider.
* **Position only:** $d$ and $c$ slide the graph without changing its shape. Example: $y = (x - 2)^4 + 5$ is $y = x^4$ moved 2 right and 5 up.
* **Reflections:** $a < 0$ reflects in the $x$-axis (e.g. $y = -x^3$); $k < 0$ reflects in the $y$-axis (e.g. $y = (-x)^3$).

rubric.point: c and d change position only

questions.text: Write equations for two different transformations of $y = x^4$ that both have vertex $({{d}}, {{c}})$, open **downward**, and are **narrower** than $y = x^4$. Explain how your parameter choices produce each property.
questions.modelAnswer:
Vertex $(d, c) = ({{d}}, {{c}})$ requires $y = a[k(x - {{d}})]^4 + {{c}}$.

Opening downward requires $a < 0$. Narrower requires a vertical stretch ($|a| > 1$) or a horizontal compression ($|k| > 1$).

Examples:
1. $y = -3(x - {{d}})^4 + {{c}}$ — vertical stretch by 3 with reflection in the $x$-axis.
2. $y = -[2(x - {{d}})]^4 + {{c}}$ — horizontal compression by $\tfrac12$ with reflection in the $x$-axis.

Both have vertex $({{d}}, {{c}})$, axis $x = {{d}}$, and range $y \le {{c}}$.

questions.text: For $y = a[k(x - d)]^n + c$, explain why an even value of $n$ gives a vertex and a restricted range, while an odd value of $n$ gives no vertex and a range of all real numbers. Refer to the graphs of $y = x^2$, $y = x^4$, $y = x^3$ and $y = x^5$.
questions.modelAnswer:
For even $n$, $x^n \ge 0$ for all $x$, with the smallest value 0 at $x = 0$. The graphs of $y = x^2$ and $y = x^4$ have a lowest point at the origin. Stretching by $a$ and shifting by $c$ makes the lowest (or, if $a<0$, highest) value $c$, at $x = d$: this point $(d, c)$ is the vertex, and the range is $y \ge c$ or $y \le c$.

For odd $n$, $x^n$ takes every real value: negative for $x<0$ and positive for $x>0$, with no turning point ($y = x^3$, $y = x^5$ always increase). Stretches and translations do not create a highest or lowest point, so the range stays $\{y \in \mathbb{R}\}$. The point $(d, c)$ is a centre of point symmetry rather than a vertex.

rubric.point: Even powers are never negative → minimum at 0
Explains vertex (d, c) and restricted range
Odd powers take all values, no turning point
Range all reals and (d, c) as centre of symmetry

questions.text: The graph of $y = x^3$ is transformed so that the point $(1, 1)$ maps to $({{d+1}}, {{c-a}})$ and the origin maps to $({{d}}, {{c}})$, with no horizontal stretch. Determine the equation of the transformed function and describe the transformations.
questions.modelAnswer:
With no horizontal stretch, $k = 1$, so $y = a(x - d)^3 + c$.

The origin maps to $(d, c) = ({{d}}, {{c}})$.

The point $(1, 1)$ maps to $(1 + d,\ a + c) = ({{d+1}},\ {{c-a}})$, so $a + {{c}} = {{c-a}}$ and $a = -{{a}}$.

$$y = -{{a}}(x - {{d}})^3 + {{c}}$$

Transformations: vertical stretch by a factor of {{a}} with a reflection in the $x$-axis, then translation {{d}} units right and {{c}} units up.

rubric.point: Uses the origin's image for d and c
